title: Surjectivity of the local product map from the completion of the localized algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S$ a finite commutative $R$-algebra [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $p$ a prime ideal. Put $A=R_p$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $B=A\otimes_R S$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $J=pB$, $Q=\{q\subset S:q\text{ prime},q\cap R=p\}$, and $D_q=\widehat{S_q}$, completed at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\psi_q:B\to S_q$ be $S$-algebra maps whose values on $r\otimes1$ equal the canonical localized maps $\varphi_q:R_p\to S_q$. Let $g:\widehat B_J\to\prod_{q\in Q}D_q$ be a ring map such that for every $q,n,x,b$, $x_n=b\bmod J^n$ implies $(g(x)_q)_n=\psi_q(b)\bmod(qS_q)^n$. Then $g$ is surjective. This is the inverse-limit product step for the localized algebra; its domain is not a tensor product with the completed base.

proof.text: Put A = R_p and B = A tensor_R S. B is finite over the Noetherian local ring A. The finitely many primes over m correspond to Q and have local rings S_q. For n > 0 the Artinian ring B/m^n B is canonically the product of the S_q/m^n S_q by Tags 00JA and 00CT. The isomorphisms commute with reduction because their maps are induced by the same localization maps at every level. The S-algebra property of psi and its prescribed values on r tensor 1 determine the localization maps on all pure tensors and hence on B.

In each S_q the m S_q-adic and maximal-ideal-adic filtrations are cofinal: m S_q is contained in q S_q, and finite generation plus radical equality gives (q S_q)^t contained in m S_q. Tag 0394 gives the canonical comparison of completions, induced by the identity on S_q.

Given a tuple in the maximal-ideal completions, use these comparisons to obtain m-adic sequences in all factors. At each positive n apply the inverse quotient product isomorphism to their coordinates. These preimages commute with reduction by uniqueness, hence define an element of the m-adic completion of B. The n = 0 coordinate belongs to the zero quotient.

The prescribed level equation for g identifies its value on the compatible preimage sequence with the chosen tuple, first in every quotient and then by completion extensionality. If Q is empty, choose zero. No comparison with a tensor product of the completed base is used.

theorem completion_localizedAlgebra_product_surjective
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    let A := Localization.AtPrime p
    let B := A ⊗[R] S
    letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := A) (B := S)
    let J := p.map (algebraMap R B)
    let Q := p.primesOver S
    let D := fun q : Q ↦
      AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1))
        (Localization.AtPrime q.1)
    ∀ (ψ : ∀ q : Q, B →ₐ[S] Localization.AtPrime q.1),
      (∀ (q : Q) (r : A), ψ q (r ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : S)) =
        Localization.localRingHom p q.1 (algebraMap R S)
          (Ideal.LiesOver.over (P := q.1) (p := p)) r) →
      ∀ (g : AdicCompletion J B →+* (∀ q : Q, D q)),
        (∀ (q : Q) (n : ℕ) (x : AdicCompletion J B) (b : B),
          evalₐ J n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n) b →
          evalₐ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1)) n (g x q) =
            Ideal.Quotient.mk
              ((IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.1)) ^ n) (ψ q b)) →
        Function.Surjective g
